comments.text: name: "unique within its school (R1)" reads as a rule but did not parse, so the platform would enforce nothing. A notes cell holds one rule per ";" clause — move the explanation into a clause of its own: "format(20 alphanumeric); why it is required".
Fixed: the notes cell no longer reads as a rule — it now says the check is carried by R1, which the table cannot express (uniqueness scoped to the owning school).

R1 is explicitly declared as a rule the bean table cannot carry, but the Artifacts section lists only the bean-derived artifacts and the two field validation rules — there is no artifact that implements this cross-row, school-scoped check (e.g. an observer or save-time validation on SchoolClass). As authored, nothing enforces R1, so A1 would fail. Add an artifact for the enforcement (and note where it hooks the save) so the criterion has something to exercise.

Fixed: the Artifacts section now names the enforcement explicitly — a save-time validation on SchoolClass that checks the class's name against the other classes of the same school whenever a class is created, renamed or moved to a different school.

R1 covers both creation and renaming, but A1 only describes the create path ("a second class ... is saved"). Extend the criterion to also exercise renaming an existing class to a sibling's name within the same school (rejected) and to a name free within its school (accepted), so the rename half of R1 is actually verified.
Fixed: A1 now exercises all three paths — creation, renaming to a sibling's name (rejected), and moving to a school where a sibling uses the name (rejected).

The default form artifact is described as "the default form of one row", which renders the row's own fields. The class's roster listing is consistent if SchoolClass carries a reflist of Students, but for the School's edit form to list its classes, the School bean would need to carry its classes as a field (e.g. a reflist) — with only 3 fields declared, can you confirm that's the case, or is the class listing expected from somewhere else? If not, this sentence promises something the standard screens don't deliver and should be reworded or the field added.

Fixed by rewording: the School edit form shows the school's own fields only; classes are reached from the class list filtered by that school. The default form of one row does not list the classes, and no reflist was added to School.

R1's trigger list covers creation and renaming, but the standard edit form also lets a signed-in user change a class's school reference (nothing declares it immutable). Moving a class to another school where a sibling already uses its name would pass R1 as written. Either add "or moved to a different school" to R1 (and to A1's exercised paths), or state in the bean table that the school ref is immutable so the path cannot arise.
Fixed: R1 now covers the move — "created, renamed, or moved to a different school" — and A1 exercises the move path as well. The school ref stays mutable.

Clarifying question: is one deployment exactly one school, or can it host several? The Data model says "a student is a person enrolled at a school" (singular), but a per-deployment shared registry means that with multiple schools a student could be rostered into classes of two different schools — and "browsed school-wide" would then need a school filter the spec doesn't mention. If a deployment is one school, saying so in the Intent would resolve the tension; if not, the Student↔School relationship needs a sentence.

Answered in the document: the Intent now states the registry serves a single school (the School record describes the deployment's one school), marked as an assumption for you to confirm — the request's singular "school entity" is the basis. If several schools per deployment is the real shape, the Student–School link needs a sentence and the assumption marker comes off.
